definition: The room created when a market leader keeps prices well above cost: rivals can price below it and still earn a return, and the leader can cut prices selectively to squeeze them. NVIDIA's ~75% gross margin is the umbrella over AI accelerators.

Running one model family, file format and toolchain across devices, edge servers and cloud racks, so a workload can move between tiers without being rewritten. A selling point for vendors with chips at every tier.
Splitting AI inference between a device (phone, PC, car) and the cloud: small or private requests run on the device's NPU, larger ones go to datacenter accelerators.

A pre-agreed observable event or metric threshold that tells you which scenario is unfolding, such as custom-ASIC revenue passing 25% of NVIDIA's Data Center revenue. Signposts turn scenarios into review triggers.

An option or warrant whose strike price equals the share price when it is granted. It has no intrinsic value at grant and pays only if the shares rise above the strike, unlike a penny warrant with a near-zero strike.
What an option or warrant would be worth if exercised today: the share price minus the strike price, times the number of shares (zero if the price is below the strike). It ignores time value.
